events.summary: PANW closed $419.91, +3.23% (Monday $406.76), its highest close in our price data (which starts 2024-10-07). It opened at $412.80 (+1.5%), reached an intraday high of $432.33 (+6.3%) and gave back about 2.9% from that high by the close (data/prices, Yahoo daily bars). Attribution: market +0.56, industry +2.14, company +0.54 points (z 0.33, normal size). The same day Reuters reported US software stocks at fresh 2026 highs: the S&P 500 software and services index rose 1.3% on Tuesday to its highest level since November 2025 as worries that AI would disrupt software faded, and the sector's expected 2026 earnings growth rose to 20.6% from 13.8% at the end of March. Reuters named CrowdStrike, Fortinet and Palo Alto as having 'triple digit percentage gains this year as companies spend heavily on cybersecurity in the age of AI'. Before Tuesday's open, Yahoo Finance's Chart of the Day said the cybersecurity fund CIBR had hit an all-time high on Monday as agentic AI adoption spurs security spending, citing Morgan Stanley's forecast that corporate cybersecurity software spending grows 23% a year through 2028 (33% if major attacks bring government mandates) and Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry: 'Agents going rogue is the biggest risk today'. No Palo Alto press release or filing on the day.

why_chain.text: Tuesday 6 Oct: PANW +3.23% to $419.91. Of that, +0.56 points came from the market, +2.14 from cybersecurity stocks and +0.54 from Palo Alto itself (normal size, z 0.33).

Why did the industry rise? Software stocks as a whole rallied: the S&P 500 software and services index rose 1.3% to its highest since November 2025; cybersecurity names were singled out for triple-digit 2026 gains.

Why did software rally? Analysts said fears that AI would replace software ('SaaSpocalypse') were overstated, and forecasts for the sector's 2026 earnings growth rose to 20.6% from 13.8% at the end of March. LPL's Adam Turnquist: 'AI has been more of an enabler for a lot of these software companies, more than a disruptor.'

Why security in particular? Investors expect AI agents (software that acts on its own) to create new things to protect; Morgan Stanley forecasts corporate cybersecurity software spending to grow 23% a year through 2028; Zscaler's CEO called rogue agents 'the biggest risk today'.

products.name: AI-agent security: Prisma AIRS (AI Runtime Security, AI Gateway) and Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense
products.what_it_is: Software and services that watch and limit what AI agents and AI models inside a company can see and do, plus an ongoing service in which Palo Alto's Unit 42 team tests a customer's systems against attacks by advanced AI models.
products.analogy: A building's security desk and key-card system, but for software robots: it checks which doors each robot may open, logs what it does, and stops it if it goes somewhere it should not.
products.buyers: Large companies and governments deploying AI agents and models.
products.how_it_works: The AI Gateway sits between agents and the models or tools they call, inspects the traffic, limits access to approved tools, removes sensitive data and tracks usage and costs. AI Runtime Security can run on NVIDIA BlueField chips, separate from the agent, so the agent cannot switch it off. Per GuruFocus, the Unit 42 service is an annual subscription that tests applications, APIs, cloud infrastructure and source-code repositories.
products.price: not disclosed (GuruFocus, 2026-10-06: the release gives neither subscription pricing nor a revenue forecast)
products.sales_source: Labelled proxy: next-generation security ARR (all of Palo Alto's newer subscription products, including AI security, cloud, SASE, Cortex and CyberArk identity) was $9.10bn at Q4 FY2026, +63% [PANW Q4 FY2026 results, 2026-09-01, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001327567/000132756726000019/ex991q426earningsrelease.htm]. No figure for the AI-security products alone.
products.stage: Prisma AIRS AI Runtime Security on NVIDIA BlueField: generally available; AI Gateway on NVIDIA Vera CPUs: future hardware [Help Net Security, 2026-09-29, https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/29/palo-alto-networks-nvidia-ai-agent-security/]. Unit 42 Frontier AI Defense launched 2026-09-22 (news log).
products.size_for_company: Unknown. Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance is $3.300-3.310bn; the AI-security products' share is not disclosed.
products.competition: CrowdStrike (also named as an NVIDIA agent-security partner), Zscaler, Cisco, Microsoft and AI-security start-ups.
products.why_investors_care: This is the product line behind the 'AI agents need security' story that moved the whole group on Tuesday (Thesis 2). Without disclosed numbers it is still a story, not revenue.
products.watch_next: Any customer count, ARR or revenue figure for AI security on the Q1 FY2027 call (mid-November); pillar 3 and trigger 3 in theses/PANW.md.
